When an issue title is edited, [update-issue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts) validates and authorizes the action, then calls `updateIssue` in [issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/server/services/issue-service.ts). The service checks the actor’s organization and permission, reads the existing issue, checks that it is live, and writes the update through `issueRepo.updateIssue`. Only after that write does it await an `issue.updated` event.

At server startup, `register` in [instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/instrumentation.ts) calls `registerEventHandlers` in [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/server/services/event-registry.ts), which calls `registerSearchListeners` in [search-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/server/services/search-service.ts). The `issue.updated` listener re-reads the persisted issue by organization and ID, then calls `indexIssue`. That calls `upsertSearchDocument` in [search-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts), replacing the existing document for the same organization, kind, and subject. The event bus’s `emit` waits for its handlers to settle, so a successful listener has indexed the new title before `updateIssue` returns. Handler failures are isolated and reported rather than rethrown, however, so a successful issue update does **not** guarantee that indexing succeeded.

The copy is the `searchIndex` table defined in [webhooks.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts). Each row holds its own ID, organization ID, subject kind and ID, optional project ID, content, and indexing timestamp. `indexIssue` stores the title and description joined by a newline; `indexProject` stores the project name and description in the same form; `indexComment` stores the comment body with no project ID. The listeners also index issue, comment, and project creation, and remove documents on issue archival, comment deletion, and project archival. An explicit `search.reindex_requested` listener handles issues. [search-reindex-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts) can re-upsert live content for an organization, but currently reads only the first page of each listing and does not remove stale documents.

There are limits to the ordinary-write coverage: `updateComment` and `updateProject` in their respective services write directly without emitting events consumed by the search listeners, so their edited text can remain stale. Likewise, archiving a project removes the project document; the listener does not itself remove documents for issues archived by the project’s cascade.

For a colleague’s search, the full-page `Page` in [search/page.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/app/(dashboard)/%5BorgSlug%5D/search/page.tsx) loads the tenant and actor, selects the permitted kinds, validates the query with `searchQuerySchema`, and calls `search` in `search-service.ts`. The schema in [search.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/schemas/search.ts) requires a 1–200 character query, valid IDs and kinds, and a page limit of 1–100. The `searchAction` in [actions/search/search.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/actions/search/search.ts) is another entry point: its `withAction` wrapper validates input and resolves the actor, then the action checks `org:read`, builds the flag context, and calls the same service. The JSON `GET` in [api/search/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/app/api/search/route.ts) also resolves the actor, checks `org:read` and the command-palette flag, validates, and calls the service.

`search` first checks organization scope and `issue:read`, then spends a token from the organization’s `search:query` bucket via `consumeRateLimit` in [rate-limit.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/lib/rate-limit.ts). It loads the organization and evaluates `advanced_search` using its plan and overrides. A request can therefore look valid yet be refused because the actor lacks access, the organization’s bucket is exhausted, or the query contains **any colon** while `advanced_search` is disabled. That flag normally requires Enterprise, though an organization override can enable it. The token is consumed before the colon check. Both the rate-limit and colon failures are plain errors, which `withAction` maps to `internal_error` through [errors.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/lib/errors.ts).

Once admitted, `searchDocuments` applies the organization filter, a SQL `LIKE '%query%'` match on content, and any kind and project filters. It counts matches, orders by indexing time and ID descending, and uses a cursor plus an extra row to build a page. `search` converts each row into a `SearchHit`: the first content line is the title, `snippetAround` extracts surrounding text, and `hrefFor` builds a kind-specific link. The action returns the hit array; the service itself also returns the total and next cursor.

The advanced syntax has an important boundary. [query-syntax.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a15341de-74d0-4761-a7e8-25790f3b57e2/src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts) parses `kind:` and `project:` in `SearchDialog` before sending the remaining text and filters. The repository itself does **not** interpret field syntax: a colon-bearing query passed directly to the service, even when the flag is enabled, is matched as literal content. Also, when the action filters requested kinds down to an empty array, the repository treats an empty array as **no kind filter**, rather than as “search no kinds.”
